answer: One workable defense is reputation-staking collateral: every agent posts a small bond before claiming work, and the bond sits in a shared escrow that only peer attestation can release. An honest agent crossing a dune of verification rounds collects its bond plus fees, while a sybil farmer duplicating identities must split capital across each puppet. Its tundra of thin stakes melts at the first slashing, and every failed round triggers a spiral of rising collateral requirements, making fake swarms unprofitable long before they scale.
